attach_buffers.md:
Binds buffers to the framebuffer.

Ensures that the `area` framebuffer object is made the current draw
and read target, and that all the required buffers for the `area`
are created and bound to the framebuffer.

This function is automatically called before emitting the
[`GLArea::render`](xref:gtk:Gtk.GLArea#event:render) signal, and doesn't normally need to be
called by application code.

get_api.brief: Gets the API that is currently in use.
get_api.md:
Gets the API that is currently in use.

If the GL area has not been realized yet, 0 is returned.

get_auto_render.brief: Returns whether the area is in auto render mode or not.
get_auto_render.md: Returns whether the area is in auto render mode or not.

get_error.brief: Gets the current error set on the `area`.
get_error.md: Gets the current error set on the `area`.

get_has_depth_buffer.brief: Returns whether the area has a depth buffer.
get_has_depth_buffer.md: Returns whether the area has a depth buffer.

get_has_stencil_buffer.brief: Returns whether the area has a stencil buffer.
get_has_stencil_buffer.md: Returns whether the area has a stencil buffer.

get_required_version.brief: Retrieves the required version of OpenGL.
get_required_version.md:
Retrieves the required version of OpenGL.

See [`GLArea.set_required_version()`](xref:gtk:Gtk.GLArea#method:set_required_version).

get_use_es.brief: Returns whether the `GtkGLArea` should use OpenGL ES.
get_use_es.md:
Returns whether the `GtkGLArea` should use OpenGL ES.

See [`GLArea.set_use_es()`](xref:gtk:Gtk.GLArea#method:set_use_es).

make_current.brief: Ensures that the `GdkGLContext` used by `area` is associated with the `GtkGLArea`.
make_current.md:
Ensures that the `GdkGLContext` used by `area` is associated with
the `GtkGLArea`.

This function is automatically called before emitting the
[`GLArea::render`](xref:gtk:Gtk.GLArea#event:render) signal, and doesn't normally need
to be called by application code.

queue_render.brief: Marks the currently rendered data (if any) as invalid, and queues a redraw of the widget.
queue_render.md:
Marks the currently rendered data (if any) as invalid, and queues
a redraw of the widget.

This ensures that the [`GLArea::render`](xref:gtk:Gtk.GLArea#event:render) signal
is emitted during the draw.

This is only needed when [`GLArea.set_auto_render()`](xref:gtk:Gtk.GLArea#method:set_auto_render) has
been called with a `FALSE` value. The default behaviour is to
emit [`GLArea::render`](xref:gtk:Gtk.GLArea#event:render) on each draw.

set_allowed_apis.brief: Sets the allowed APIs to create a context with.
set_allowed_apis.md:
Sets the allowed APIs to create a context with.

You should check [`GLArea:api`](xref:gtk:Gtk.GLArea#property:api) before drawing
with either API.

By default, all APIs are allowed.

set_auto_render.brief: Sets whether the `GtkGLArea` is in auto render mode.
set_auto_render.md:
Sets whether the `GtkGLArea` is in auto render mode.

If `auto_render` is `TRUE` the [`GLArea::render`](xref:gtk:Gtk.GLArea#event:render) signal will
be emitted every time the widget draws. This is the default and is
useful if drawing the widget is faster.

If `auto_render` is `FALSE` the data from previous rendering is kept
around and will be used for drawing the widget the next time,
unless the window is resized. In order to force a rendering
[`GLArea.queue_render()`](xref:gtk:Gtk.GLArea#method:queue_render) must be called. This mode is
useful when the scene changes seldom, but takes a long time to redraw.

set_error.brief: Sets an error on the area which will be shown instead of the GL rendering.
set_error.md:
Sets an error on the area which will be shown instead of the
GL rendering.

This is useful in the [`GLArea::create-context`](xref:gtk:Gtk.GLArea#event:create-context)
signal if GL context creation fails.

set_has_depth_buffer.brief: Sets whether the `GtkGLArea` should use a depth buffer.
set_has_depth_buffer.md:
Sets whether the `GtkGLArea` should use a depth buffer.

If `has_depth_buffer` is `TRUE` the widget will allocate and
enable a depth buffer for the target framebuffer. Otherwise
there will be none.

set_has_stencil_buffer.brief: Sets whether the `GtkGLArea` should use a stencil buffer.
set_has_stencil_buffer.md:
Sets whether the `GtkGLArea` should use a stencil buffer.

If `has_stencil_buffer` is `TRUE` the widget will allocate and
enable a stencil buffer for the target framebuffer. Otherwise
there will be none.

set_required_version.brief: Sets the required version of OpenGL to be used when creating the context for the widget.
set_required_version.md:
Sets the required version of OpenGL to be used when creating
the context for the widget.

This function must be called before the area has been realized.

set_use_es.brief: Sets whether the `area` should create an OpenGL or an OpenGL ES context.
set_use_es.md:
Sets whether the `area` should create an OpenGL or an OpenGL ES context.

You should check the capabilities of the `GdkGLContext` before drawing
with either API.

auto-render.brief: If set to `TRUE` the ::render signal will be emitted every time the widget draws.
auto-render.md:
If set to `TRUE` the ::render signal will be emitted every time
the widget draws.

This is the default and is useful if drawing the widget is faster.

If set to `FALSE` the data from previous rendering is kept around and will
be used for drawing the widget the next time, unless the window is resized.
In order to force a rendering [`GLArea.queue_render()`](xref:gtk:Gtk.GLArea#method:queue_render) must be called.
This mode is useful when the scene changes seldom, but takes a long time
to redraw.

context.md:
The `GdkGLContext` used by the `GtkGLArea` widget.

The `GtkGLArea` widget is responsible for creating the `GdkGLContext`
instance. If you need to render with other kinds of buffers (stencil,
depth, etc), use render buffers.

has-depth-buffer.brief: If set to `TRUE` the widget will allocate and enable a depth buffer for the target framebuffer.
has-depth-buffer.md:
If set to `TRUE` the widget will allocate and enable a depth buffer for the
target framebuffer.

Setting this property will enable GL's depth testing as a side effect. If
you don't need depth testing, you should call `glDisable(GL_DEPTH_TEST)`
in your `GtkGLArea::render` handler.

has-stencil-buffer.brief: If set to `TRUE` the widget will allocate and enable a stencil buffer for the target framebuffer.
has-stencil-buffer.md:
If set to `TRUE` the widget will allocate and enable a stencil buffer for the
target framebuffer.

use-es.brief: If set to `TRUE` the widget will try to create a `GdkGLContext` using OpenGL ES instead of OpenGL.
use-es.md:
If set to `TRUE` the widget will try to create a `GdkGLContext` using
OpenGL ES instead of OpenGL.

create-context.brief: Emitted when the widget is being realized.
create-context.md:
Emitted when the widget is being realized.

This allows you to override how the GL context is created.
This is useful when you want to reuse an existing GL context,
or if you want to try creating different kinds of GL options.

If context creation fails then the signal handler can use
[`GLArea.set_error()`](xref:gtk:Gtk.GLArea#method:set_error) to register a more detailed error
of how the construction failed.

render.brief: Emitted every time the contents of the `GtkGLArea` should be redrawn.
render.md:
Emitted every time the contents of the `GtkGLArea` should be redrawn.

The `context` is bound to the `area` prior to emitting this function,
and the buffers are painted to the window once the emission terminates.

resize.brief: Emitted once when the widget is realized, and then each time the widget is changed while realized.
resize.md:
Emitted once when the widget is realized, and then each time the widget
is changed while realized.

This is useful in order to keep GL state up to date with the widget size,
like for instance camera properties which may depend on the width/height
ratio.

The GL context for the area is guaranteed to be current when this signal
is emitted.

The default handler sets up the GL viewport.
